constraints: Both lookups refer to the same route row in this merge operation.
A conflict requires an explicit resolution before save.

details.mechanismOrProperty: The identity map makes both paths observe the same route instance; the unit of work holds the edit until the merge is resolved.
details.scenarioApplication: The route opened by the tile search and by ID is the same persisted route within this merge operation.
details.errorCorrection: Saving a duplicate or each edit can overwrite accepted geometry before the user chooses a conflict result.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: The map is scoped to this merge, not shared across users or future operations.
details.transfer: When an operation reaches one record through several paths, keep one in-memory identity and stage its accepted changes.

messages.text: Two in-memory copies of one route can diverge and let a later write silently replace accepted geometry.
Identity continuity is needed within this merge; a process-wide map would also share edits across unrelated operations.
The prompt requires conflict resolution before save, so immediate writes can persist a rejected edit.
Saving the last-loaded copy can discard the geometry edit from the other path instead of presenting the required conflict for explicit resolution.

feedback.reason: The two retrieval paths point to one persisted route in one merge, and geometry cannot be saved until a conflict is resolved. Reuse that operation’s instance and track its change through the chosen save.

options.text: Let the tile search create another route object and save whichever copy was loaded last.
Keep every route in a process-wide identity map shared by all user operations.
Resolve route ID and tile search to one route instance; track geometry until explicit conflict resolution.
Write every geometry point to storage as soon as the editor changes it.
Save whichever route instance was loaded last, so the tile-search copy overwrites the geometry edit when the merge unit commits.

prompt: A cartographer edits a route offline. During one merge command, the editor loads the same route by route ID and again through a tile search; a conflict must be shown, never silently overwrite accepted geometry. What object-handling approach supports that command?

constraints: Both code paths resolve the same character in one command.
Inventory and campaign score changes are saved after reward validation.

details.mechanismOrProperty: Identity resolution avoids competing character copies, while the unit of work tracks the changes made during validation.
details.scenarioApplication: The reward rule and screen inspect one character while the inventory and score changes are pending.
details.errorCorrection: Saving before validation or splitting screen and rule writes can persist a partial reward.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: The useful identity scope is one command; no fact supports a process-wide character cache.
details.transfer: Within one business operation, resolve duplicate loads consistently and commit its accepted changes as a unit.

messages.text: The copies can disagree about the same inventory and score changes.
The rule must validate before the reward changes are saved.
The prompt needs one identity during this command, not shared mutable state across separate commands.
Separate copies and writes can leave inventory changed without the matching campaign score, contrary to the post-validation outcome.

feedback.reason: Both reads identify one character during the same command, and reward validation precedes persistence. Keep one instance and collect the accepted changes before writing them.

options.text: Keep one character copy for the reward screen and another for the campaign rule, then write both.
Persist the inventory change before checking whether the reward is legal in the campaign.
Retain the character instance in a singleton across later campaign commands.
Let the reward screen save its character copy first, then have the campaign rule update score in a later write.
Return one character for both reads and track validated inventory and score together.

prompt: In a campaign manager, applying a reward changes a character’s inventory and campaign score. The command loads that character through both the reward screen and the campaign rule; both reads identify the same character row. What should the persistence session do?

constraints: The map and planner refer to one shipment in the reassignment.
Carrier validation occurs before any write.

details.mechanismOrProperty: The unit of work holds the validated change on the same shipment instance used by the map path.
details.scenarioApplication: The map path and dispatch path resolve to the shipment being reassigned, not independent shipment records.
details.errorCorrection: Writing a carrier field before checking its restrictions exposes an invalid transition; reconciling after both writes is too late.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: The shipment identity requirement applies to one operation, not all dispatch requests.
details.transfer: Use operation-scoped identity and deferred persistence when one validation governs several field changes.

messages.text: The map and planner would then hold competing versions of the same shipment during one operation.
That can leave the shipment assigned to a carrier that violates its validated restrictions.
Identity Map consistency is needed within this operation; sharing mutable instances across requests risks stale edits.
Saving both copies before reconciling allows the same shipment to retain conflicting carrier or handoff values.

feedback.reason: The two paths load the same shipment during one reassignment, and validation must precede persistence. One operation-scoped instance lets the accepted carrier and handoff state be tracked together.

options.text: Let the map keep its own shipment instance and save the planner’s copy immediately.
Use one shipment instance; track carrier and handoff until validation succeeds.
Persist the carrier field first, then check temperature limits and handoff ownership.
Reuse one shipment object across all dispatch requests for the day.
Save both map and planner shipment copies, then reconcile any carrier disagreement in the next dispatch report.

prompt: A dispatch planner reassigns a shipment to a carrier. The temperature limit and carrier handoff owner are fields on the same shipment record; the operation validates the new carrier before saving. A map view also loads the shipment by ID during that operation. Which persistence behavior fits?

constraints: The two reads identify one account during this allocation.
Balance and allocation record must agree when saved.

details.mechanismOrProperty: One identity ensures both services calculate and record against the same loaded balance; the unit of work gathers the update and insertion.
details.scenarioApplication: The allocation’s account balance and ledger entry describe the same repayment result.
details.errorCorrection: Writing only one side first risks mismatched ledger state, and a negative balance is explicitly disallowed.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: The identity map is per allocation operation rather than a global mutable cache.
details.transfer: When a business action updates an object and adds its corresponding record, track both before completing persistence.

messages.text: Separate copies can calculate against different balances and leave the allocation record inconsistent with the saved account balance.
A failure between writes leaves a balance change with no matching allocation record.
The nonnegative balance is an immediate condition, not a later reporting correction.
The prompt requires one identity within this allocation, not shared account state across concurrent operations.

feedback.reason: The repeated account ID is one account within this allocation, and its final balance must match the allocation record without going below zero. Track the account and inserted record in one work unit after calculation.

options.text: Load separate account copies for principal and interest, apply each portion independently, then reconcile their balances in the ledger.
Save the reduced balance before inserting the allocation record.
Apply the repayment even if it makes the balance negative, then reconcile the ledger later.
Track one account’s balance with its matching allocation in a single work unit.
Share a mutable account object among all repayment operations.

prompt: A lending ledger allocates one repayment across principal and interest. The resulting outstanding balance cannot be negative, and the allocation record must match the balance change. The repository reads the account once, then the allocation service reads the same account ID again. How should the operation manage these changes?

constraints: The match result and next bracket participant are one local accepted outcome.
Player notification is sent after the local update.

details.mechanismOrProperty: The unit of work gathers the match and bracket updates before the notification is sent.

details.errorCorrection: A separate bracket write can expose inconsistent progression, while an external acknowledgement is not part of the local persistence commit.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: No fact requires loading or locking unrelated matches in the tournament.
details.transfer: Use a unit of work for the local set of changes that form one accepted result; perform later external effects separately.

messages.text: Players could receive a result that storage has not accepted.
The result and next participant could diverge between writes even though the prompt defines them as one accepted match outcome.
Notification is an external follow-up; the prompt does not say it shares the local persistence transaction.
Only this match and its immediate bracket update participate in the described result.

feedback.reason: The local result consists of a forfeited match and the corresponding next bracket participant; the notification follows after the local update. Track those two changes together without extending persistence across the network.

options.text: Track match and bracket outcome together; notify after the local commit.
Send the forfeit notice before persisting the match result and bracket change.
Save the forfeit result first and advance the bracket participant in a second, uncoordinated write.
Keep the database transaction open until every player notification is acknowledged.
Load and track every match in the tournament before a single forfeit can be committed.

prompt: A tournament official forfeits a match after timeout. The match result and the bracket’s next participant must reflect one legal match outcome; the persistence API can commit these local updates together. A notification to players is sent afterward. What should the unit of work include?

constraints: Both paths identify the same revision row.
The seal does not move to the document’s latest revision.

details.errorCorrection: Loading the latest revision or replacing the seal target would change the notarized content.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Object reuse is limited to the request; it does not turn revision objects into a global cache.

messages.text: That substitutes a different immutable revision for the exact one named by the seal.
Two instances for the same row can drift within one request and confuse which revision the seal refers to.
The requirement is same identity within this request, not indefinite mutable reuse across requests.
The prompt says the seal retains an exact immutable revision, not whichever object was loaded last.

feedback.reason: Both lookups name the same immutable revision in one request. Reusing one request-scoped instance preserves that reference without substituting the latest revision.

options.text: Let history load the document’s latest revision even when the seal lookup returned its named earlier revision.
Construct separate revision objects for the two paths and let each apply its own edits.
Return one revision identity from both lookups for the signing request.
Keep every revision loaded by all signing requests in one process-wide map.
Update the seal to reference the object most recently loaded by either path.

prompt: A document notarization service loads a sealed revision through both a seal lookup and a document-history view during one signing request. The seal names an exact immutable revision. What should those two paths return?

constraints: The result and both revision links are written as one completed snapshot.
The report is a later projection.

details.mechanismOrProperty: The unit of work collects the new object and relationship writes until the complete snapshot can be stored.
details.scenarioApplication: The result row and its two revision relationships together describe one publishable snapshot.
details.errorCorrection: Publishing before the links exist or replacing them with latest revisions loses required provenance.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: The report is downstream, and an in-memory process map cannot replace a durable published result.
details.transfer: Track all local records that make one published artifact complete before marking it published.

messages.text: That exposes a published result without the exact inputs the scenario requires.
The report is built later and does not define whether the snapshot has its revision links.
The result would no longer identify the exact dataset and code revisions used for its snapshot.
A later request needs the persisted published snapshot; shared unsaved mutable state is not a persistence record.

feedback.reason: A publishable result includes both exact revision links, so the unit of work must track the new result and links before publication completes. The later report consumes that completed snapshot.

options.text: Publish the result row first and insert revision links in later calls.
Include the future report build in the same write unit as snapshot publication.
Keep the revision links only in memory, then replace them with whichever revisions are latest when the result is persisted.
Keep unsaved snapshot objects in a process-wide map for future requests.
Track the result and both revision links; publish only when the snapshot is complete.

prompt: An experiment owner publishes a result snapshot. The write creates a result row and two links to exact dataset and code revisions; the result may be published only if both links are present. A report is built later. What does the unit of work track?

constraints: Comment persistence establishes the accepted comment before notification.
Provider failure does not undo the comment.

details.mechanismOrProperty: The unit of work persists the complete comment relationship; notification handling can observe the accepted comment afterward.

details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Keep author and revision in the accepted record; do not widen the local transaction to the notification provider.
details.transfer: Separate a durable local decision from a subsequent external notification when their success conditions differ.

messages.text: A provider outage would prevent the valid accepted comment from being recorded.
The prompt makes notification failure independent of the comment’s validity.
The accepted comment must retain both references at acceptance.
The prompt says provider failure does not undo the accepted comment; rollback would discard valid local state because of a separate effect.

feedback.reason: The comment is locally valid once its body, author, and revision are committed; delivery is a later external effect. Record the comment before attempting notification.

options.text: Send the notification first and persist the comment only after the provider confirms.
Commit the comment and author/revision links before separate notification.
Keep the local database transaction open until the notification provider confirms delivery.
Save the comment body now and add its author and revision in a later cleanup.
Roll back the accepted comment and its references whenever notification fails, so the database and provider appear consistent.

prompt: An annotation editor accepts a comment. The comment must retain the author and document revision; a notification is sent only after the comment is committed. If the notification provider is unavailable, the accepted comment remains valid. What is the appropriate save sequence?

constraints: All required evidence and the complete state belong to one submission outcome.

details.errorCorrection: Completing before evidence is present or ignoring failed evidence writes violates the submission rule.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: An incomplete inspection remains retryable rather than being deleted or treated as complete.
details.transfer: A unit of work should collect the local changes that support a state transition before recording that transition.

messages.text: That exposes the complete state before all required evidence is present.
The required set may be incomplete, so separate writes cannot justify the complete state.
The prompt explicitly defines retryable as the incomplete outcome.
A notification says nothing about whether the required evidence rows are present.

feedback.reason: Completeness depends on the full required evidence set, while retryable represents the valid incomplete case. Collect the evidence and state transition before recording completion.

options.text: Mark the submission complete, then add missing evidence in the next request.
Commit evidence rows independently, then mark the submission complete even if only some writes succeeded.
Delete the inspection whenever evidence is incomplete instead of leaving it retryable.
Track evidence and completion together; mark complete only after required evidence passes.
Use a notification delivery receipt as proof that all evidence was persisted.

prompt: A field inspection has evidence rows and a submission state. It becomes complete only when all required evidence is present; otherwise it stays explicitly retryable. Several evidence rows are added before the user submits. Which work should be collected before marking complete?

constraints: The new invoice and its rejected-invoice reference are recorded together.

details.boundaryOrTradeoff: No external payment atomicity or timeout guarantee is stated.

Payment is a later request and no shared local/external transaction is specified.
The new issue would be persisted without the required link during the interval before the later job.
The prompt says the reissue is saved before payment is requested, so provider outcome does not define its local identity.

feedback.reason: The local reissue is complete when the new invoice and its link to the rejected issue are recorded. The payment request follows and does not replace that local work unit.

options.text: Save the new invoice with its rejected-issue reference before requesting payment.
Overwrite the rejected invoice row with the new issue and remove its prior ID.
Hold the invoice transaction open until the payment provider confirms.
Save the reissue now and attach its rejected-invoice reference in a later audit job.

prompt: A billing operator reissues a rejected invoice. The new issue must reference the rejected invoice ID, and the payment request is made only after the reissue is saved. Rejected invoices remain in the audit history. Which changes belong in the local work unit?

constraints: Both loads identify the same badge during one access request.

details.errorCorrection: A stale employee-list copy could permit access; checking after grant reverses the required order.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: The prompt does not require a global cache or audit projection in the authorization path.

messages.text: The grant path could then observe the stale copy and authorize access after revocation.
The needed identity is within one request; cross-request mutable sharing is not required and can leak stale state.
Refreshing afterward is too late: the access decision must observe revocation before granting.
The prompt names the access request’s badge state as authority, not a separate audit view.

feedback.reason: Both reads resolve the same badge in one access operation, and revocation must be seen before entry is granted. One request-scoped identity avoids divergent badge copies.

options.text: Let the employee list hold its own badge copy while the direct lookup updates another.
Share mutable badge entities globally across all door requests.
Resolve one badge per request; check revocation before granting access.
Grant from the employee-list copy first, then refresh badge state through the direct lookup afterward.
Wait for the audit projection to update before using either badge object.

prompt: A facilities administrator revokes a badge. In one access request, the badge is loaded by badge ID and again through the employee’s active-badge list; revocation must be visible before that request grants entry. What identity scope matters?

constraints: Label record and approved revision link are saved before print attempts.

prompt: A shipping operator approves a shipment revision and requests a label. The label record must link to that approved revision; printing can be retried after the record is saved. Which work unit should the application use?

options.text: Save the new room before validating whether its interval has capacity.
Track room and interval after capacity validation; calculate fees later.
Include fee calculation and its service call in the booking persistence transaction.
Change the room now but keep the old interval until a background job updates it later.

prompt: A rehearsal move changes the booking’s room and its reserved interval. The scheduler validates destination capacity before accepting the move; a cancellation fee is calculated later by another service. What should the unit of work track?

The prompt identifies one exhibit controller’s state, not a global mode.

options.text: Use one lesson instance; retire it without changing progress identity.

prompt: A curriculum editor retires a lesson. Existing progress continues to reference the stable lesson ID, and the lesson is loaded once by the editor and once through a learner-progress view during the same command. Which object behavior is needed?

constraints: Both paths identify one listing in this command.
